page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Enhanced family, driven by the KVM hypervisor. The instance is powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock of 2.9 GHz. It is provisioned with 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. Cache allocation comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 48 MB L3 cache. Hardware instruction extensions include AVX-512 with VNNI support, AES-NI, and SHA-NI cryptographic accelerators. The instance includes 16.0 GB of memory, providing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. It features no local storage and does not include bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying on external network-attached storage and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations reveal balanced single-core execution alongside constrained multi-core throughput due to the 2-core physical limit. Single-core stress-ng tests reached 1879.48, and Geekbench single-core scored 1556.0, both positioning in the middle 50% tier. Cryptographic and compression tests also aligned in the average band, with single-threaded gzip hitting 27.8 GB/sec and PassMark CPU encryption scoring 3641.77. In contrast, multi-threaded tasks show performance limitations: stress-ng multi-core reached 3870.6, Geekbench multi-core recorded 3338.0, and PassMark CPU totaled 5868.95, all placing in the bottom 25%. Uncached large-block memory bandwidth demonstrated 30.13 GB/sec read and 24.19 GB/sec write speeds, with multi-threaded bzip3 decompression dropping into the bottom 10% at 21.15 GB/sec.

Given its hardware baseline, the ecs.g7se.xlarge provides entry-tier resource density for environments that do not require heavy parallel computational throughput or local disk IOPS. The presence of AVX-512 VNNI assists lightweight quantized inference, achieving 109.67 tokens per second on small 135M parameter language models during text generation. Because there is no bundled local storage and static web serving tops out at 6.17 GB/sec, operational setups must pair this instance with network volumes. It is best configured for moderate general-purpose workloads, including standard web serving, lightweight application backends, development environments, and modular microservices.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose compute instance featuring 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by an Intel Xeon 8369B processor at 2.9 GHz. Operating on the KVM hypervisor with x86_64 architecture, it incorporates AVX-512 VNNI and hardware crypto acceleration. The instance has no bundled local storage, lacks dedicated GPUs, and provides a 2 Gbps baseline network throughput. Performance benchmarks display average single-core capabilities, including a 1556.0 Geekbench score and 27.8 GB/sec gzip compression, alongside lower-tier multi-core and memory bandwidth results like 3870.6 on multi-core stress-ng. The lack of onboard NVMe storage necessitates external cloud disks for persistent state. Offering a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, ecs.g7se.xlarge functions effectively for general application hosting, microservices, staging environments, and light utility tasks.
